summary: Grays Harbor County, WA state lookout: a 1942 Aircraft Warning station cabin, a 40-foot DNR tower from 1954 removed or destroyed by 1968; summit now a gravel pit.

facts.design: Two-story 10 by 10 foot Cowen-type cabin (1942), then a 40-foot wooden DNR live-in tower (1954)
facts.status_note: Tower removed or destroyed by 1968; house torn down by 1970; most of the summit now a gravel pit

access.note: Willhite Web says a private timberlands permit is officially needed for the hike; the watershed gate is open late April to October or Labor Day

visit.trail_note: 1.6 miles one way on foot from Failor Lake, along a gated watershed road with a creek crossing

events.note: Two-story 10 by 10 foot Cowen-type cabin, the first lookout on the site
Aircraft Warning Service station activated March 28, 1942 (Olympia Filter Center)
Aircraft Warning Service use ended; state keeps the site for its original purpose
Closed for the season September 13 because of fog; Frances Getty of Copalis Beach tended it
Cabin replaced by a 40-foot wooden DNR live-in tower
Forest Lookouts quotes a May 30, 1957 report that the lookout was now in operation; Dorothy Smith of Porter on duty
Tower removed or destroyed; register and Forest Lookouts say removed, firelookout.com says destroyed
USGS reports the lookout house torn down with no plans to replace it

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Forest Lookouts page say removed; firelookout.com says destroyed; Willhite Web says removed or destroyed. Not resolved; the story reports the disagreement.
Willhite Web spells the access lake both Fallar Lake and Failor Lake. The story uses Failor Lake, the spelling in the same page's access text.

notes_for_editor: Height 12.2 m is the 40-foot 1954 tower; the 1942 cabin is about 25 feet per a 1953 USGS note quoted by Willhite Web but is not recorded in facts. Staffing as_of is the last year named in our reading (1957). Access level 'permission' is taken from Willhite Web's note on the private timberlands permit; no agency statement was read. The summit's current status is described only by Willhite Web's 2020 visit.
